Borrowing pulls noisy estimates toward truth, held-likelihood C-index improve:
code: simulate <- function(n, beta, alpha) {   x <- matrix(rnorm(n * length(beta)), n, dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("x", seq_along(beta))))   h <- 1 - exp(-exp(outer(drop(x %*% beta), alpha, "+")))   hit <- matrix(runif(length(h)), n) < h   first <- apply(hit, 1, function(r) if (any(r)) which(r)[1] else NA)   interval <- ifelse(is.na(first), length(alpha), first); event <- as.integer(!is.na(first))   censor <- sample.int(length(alpha), n, replace = TRUE)   cens <- censor < interval; interval[cens] <- censor[cens]; event[cens] <- 0L   list(x = x, interval = interval, event = event) } set.seed(11) beta_true <- c(0.7, -0.6, 0.5, -0.4, 0.3, 0, 0, 0) alpha     <- seq(-2.6, -1.8, length.out = 6) cohort <- simulate(120, beta_true, alpha) test   <- simulate(3000, beta_true, alpha)  registry <- release_model(beta     = c(x1 = 0.8, x2 = -0.5, x3 = 0.6, x4 = -0.3, x5 = 0.3),                           baseline = exp(alpha) * 1.25) target_dt <- target_discrete(cohort$interval, cohort$event, cohort$x)  dt_own <- cv.bregsurv(target_dt) dt_kl  <- cv.bregsurv(target_dt, registry) round(rbind(truth = beta_true, target_only = coef(dt_own), kullback_leibler = coef(dt_kl)), 2) #>                    x1    x2   x3    x4   x5    x6   x7    x8 #> truth            0.70 -0.60 0.50 -0.40 0.30  0.00 0.00  0.00 #> target_only      1.23 -1.00 0.21 -0.52 0.28 -0.33 0.35 -0.01 #> kullback_leibler 0.96 -0.67 0.42 -0.39 0.30 -0.13 0.14 -0.01 held_out <- function(fit) {   h <- predict(fit, test$x, type = "hazard")   y <- matrix(0, nrow(h), ncol(h)); ev <- which(test$event == 1); y[cbind(ev, test$interval[ev])] <- 1   at_risk <- outer(test$interval, seq_len(ncol(h)), ">=")   c(nll = -mean(rowSums(at_risk * (y * log(h) + (1 - y) * log1p(-h)))),     c_index = cindex(rowSums(-log1p(-h)), test$interval, test$event)) } round(rbind(target_only = held_out(dt_own), kullback_leibler = held_out(dt_kl)), 3) #>                    nll c_index #> target_only      1.024   0.761 #> kullback_leibler 0.893   0.782

text: Proposition (Exact Ties). stratified Cox model exact ties, integrated objective \(Q_{\eta}(\boldsymbol{\beta}) = -\ell(\boldsymbol{\beta}) + \eta\,\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mathbf{P}\parallel\mathbf{Q})\) admits representation \[ Q_{\eta}(\boldsymbol{\beta}) \propto -\sum_{s=1}^{S} \sum_{k=1}^{K^{(s)}} \left\{ \frac{ r_k(\mathcal{D}_k^{(s)};\boldsymbol{\beta}) + \eta \sum_{H \\mathcal{R}_k^{(s)}(d_k^{(s)})} \mathbf{p}_k^{(s)}(H)\,r_k(H;\boldsymbol{\beta}) }{1+\eta} - \log \left[ \sum_{H'\\mathcal{R}_k^{(s)}(d_k^{(s)})} \exp\!\bigl(r_k(H';\boldsymbol{\beta})\bigr) \right] \right\}, \] \(r_k(\mathcal{D}_k^{(s)};\boldsymbol{\beta}) = \sum_{j\\mathcal{D}_k^{(s)}} r(\mathbf{Z}_j^{(s)},\boldsymbol{\beta})\). Furthermore, linear specification \(r(\mathbf{Z}_j^{(s)},\boldsymbol{\beta}) = {\mathbf{Z}_j^{(s)}}^\top\boldsymbol{\beta}\), define \[ \mathbf{w}_{\mathcal{D}_k}^{(s)} = \sum_{j\\mathcal{D}_k^{(s)}} \mathbf{Z}_j^{(s)}, \qquad \mathbf{w}_H^{(s)} = \sum_{j\H} \mathbf{Z}_j^{(s)}, \qquad \tilde{\mathbf{w}}_{k}^{(s)} = \sum_{H\\mathcal{R}_k^{(s)}(d_k^{(s)})} \mathbf{p}_k^{(s)}(H)\,\mathbf{w}_H^{(s)}. \] objective simplifies \[ Q_{\eta}(\boldsymbol{\beta}) \propto -\sum_{s=1}^{S} \sum_{k=1}^{K^{(s)}} \left\{ \left( \frac{ \mathbf{w}_{\mathcal{D}_k}^{(s)} + \eta\,\tilde{\mathbf{w}}_{k}^{(s)} }{1+\eta} \right)^\top \boldsymbol{\beta} - \log \left[ \sum_{H'\\mathcal{R}_k^{(s)}(d_k^{(s)})} \exp\!\bigl( {\mathbf{w}_{H'}^{(s)}}^\top\boldsymbol{\beta} \bigr) \right] \right\}. \]

title: Extension: tied event times
text: Although Cox’s exact method provides precise treatment tied failure times, computational cost grows combinatorially number ties event time: size candidate failure set \(\binom{n_k^{(s)}}{d_k^{(s)}}\) becomes prohibitively large whenever \(d_k^{(s)}\) non-negligible relative \(n_k^{(s)}\). Breslow approximation (Breslow 1974) addresses limitation replacing exact combinatorial denominator computationally tractable surrogate, retaining support \(\mathcal{R}_k^{(s)}(d_k^{(s)})\) size-\(d_k^{(s)}\) subsets risk set.

text: Every estimator package minimizes \[ Q_\eta(\theta) = -\ell(\theta) + \eta\,\mathcal{B}_G(\theta), \qquad \eta \ge 0, \] \(\ell\) cohort’s log-likelihood \(\mathcal{B}_G\) Bregman divergence model external one. objective separates three decisions, package one object : release fixes generator \(G\), divergence: release can also enter every level (records yield coefficients, coefficients yield risk score), data can compare several members. Every linear target takes ridge, lasso elastic-net penalty, penalty path built \(\eta\).

code: library(BregSurv) data(ExampleData_lowdim) tr <- ExampleData_lowdim$train  target  <- target_cox(time = tr$time, event = tr$status, z = tr$z) release <- release_coef(ExampleData_lowdim$beta_external_poor)   # a published model on 2 of 6 covariates  kl  <- cv.bregsurv(target, release, member = "kl") euc <- cv.bregsurv(target, release, member = "mahalanobis") own <- cv.bregsurv(target)                                        # your data alone  # one partition, one criterion: the cross-validated losses compare directly (lower is better) c(target_only = own$value, kullback_leibler = kl$value, euclidean = euc$value) #>      target_only kullback_leibler        euclidean #>            2.625            2.513            2.520 cv.bregsurv(target_ncc(case, set, z), release_coef(beta), member = "kl", penalty = "lasso") cv.bregsurv(target_discrete(interval, event, z), release_model(beta, baseline = dH0)) cv.bregsurv(target_discrete(interval, event, z, score = nn_score()), release_model(beta, baseline = dH0))

code: # Six internal covariates; the external source estimated only four of them. z <- matrix(seq_len(30), nrow = 5, ncol = 6,             dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("Z", 1:6))) beta_ext <- c(Z1 = 0.30, Z3 = 0.25, Z5 = -0.10, Z6 = 0.05)  # Z2 and Z4 are absent from the external vector and are zero-padded. align_beta(z, beta_ext) #> 2 covariate(s) absent from external 'beta' were set to 0: Z2, Z4. #>    Z1    Z2    Z3    Z4    Z5    Z6  #>  0.30  0.00  0.25  0.00 -0.10  0.05   # A one-column matrix is accepted; its row names are used as the names. beta_mat <- matrix(c(0.30, 0.25, -0.10, 0.05), ncol = 1,                    dimnames = list(c("Z1", "Z3", "Z5", "Z6"), "coef")) align_beta(z, beta_mat) #> 2 covariate(s) absent from external 'beta' were set to 0: Z2, Z4. #>    Z1    Z2    Z3    Z4    Z5    Z6  #>  0.30  0.00  0.25  0.00 -0.10  0.05   # An unnamed beta is aligned positionally and must have length ncol(z). align_beta(z, c(0.30, 0, 0.25, 0, -0.10, 0.05)) #>    Z1    Z2    Z3    Z4    Z5    Z6  #>  0.30  0.00  0.25  0.00 -0.10  0.05

Cross-validation performed stratum level: matched set treated indivisible unit assigned single fold using get_fold_cc. ensures conditional likelihood well-defined within training test split. cv.criteria argument controls CV performance metric: "loss": Average negative conditional log-likelihood held-data, normalized per observation. fold, conditional log-likelihood computed test matched sets using fitted \(\hat\beta\) corresponding training data divided number held-observations fold; resulting fold-wise losses averaged (unweighted) across folds. "AUC": matched-set AUC based within-stratum comparisons. stratum, case score compared control scores, counting concordant/discordant/tied pairs aggregating across strata. Higher AUC indicates better discrimination. "CIndex": Alias "AUC". 1:m matched case–control setting, matched-set AUC equivalent conditional concordance index, computed using path "AUC". "Brier": conditional Brier score based within-stratum softmax probabilities. stratum, probability assigned member via \(\hat p_{si} = \exp(\eta_{si}) / \sum_{j \S_s} \exp(\eta_{sj})\), Brier score mean squared error \((Y_{si} - \hat p_{si})^2\) across observations. Lower Brier indicates better conditional calibration sharpness. returned object structure "cv.coxkl" objects cv.coxkl_ties, facilitating downstream code reuse.

title: Estimate the Baseline Cumulative Hazard for a Cox Fit — get_baseline_hazard
text: Within stratum estimator $$\hat\Lambda_0(t) = \sum_{t_k \le t}       \frac{d_k}{\sum_{j:\, T_j \ge t_k} \exp(Z_j^\top \beta)},$$ \(t_1 < t_2 < \cdots\) distinct observed event times \(d_k\) number events \(t_k\) (Breslow handling ties). risk set weighted \(\exp(Z^\top\beta)\), returned quantity baseline hazard supplied model rather marginal (Nelson-Aalen) hazard sample; two coincide beta zero. returned function right-continuous step function: \(0\) first event time constant \(\hat\Lambda_0\) last event time thereafter. stratum containing events yields identically-zero baseline rather error.

title: Conditional Logistic Regression with KL Divergence (CLR-KL) — ncckl
text: function maps Conditional Logistic Regression problem Cox Proportional Hazards model fixed event time \(T=1\) event indicator \(\delta=y\). utilizes coxkl_ties core engine perform data integration via KL divergence penalty. what: Simulate stratified Cox PH survival data with flexible censoring, optional binary covariates, and optional ties — sim.cox.highdim
title: Simulate stratified Cox PH survival data with flexible censoring, optional binary covariates, and optional ties — sim.cox.highdim
text: Internal function generate time--event data stratified Cox proportional hazards model high-dimensional covariates, stratum-specific multiplicative baseline scaling, controllable random censoring. Event times generated inverse transform sampling using baseline cumulative hazard. model $$h(t \mid Z, s) = \gamma_s \, h_0(t)\, \exp(Z^\top \beta),$$ \(\gamma_s\) stratum-specific positive constant, \(h_0(t)\) baseline hazard, \(\beta\) coefficient vector. Supported baseline hazards: "exponential": \(h_0(t)=1\), \(H_0(t)=t\). "weibull": \(h_0(t)=\alpha t\) \(\alpha>0\), \(H_0(t)=\alpha t^2/2\). Censoring implemented $$T_{\mathrm{obs}} = \min(T, C, \texttt{max_time}),$$ \(C\) random censoring time drawn specified distribution calibrated approximately match target censoring rate. Supported random censoring distributions: "uniform": \(C \sim \mathrm{Unif}(0, c_{\max})\). "exponential": \(C \sim \mathrm{Exp}(\lambda_c)\). "weibull": \(C \sim \mathrm{Weibull}(k, \lambda_c)\), shape \(k\) specified censor_weibull_shape. "lognormal": \(C \sim \mathrm{LogNormal}(\mu_c, \sigma_c^2)\), \(\sigma_c\) specified censor_lognormal_sdlog. "none": random censoring; administrative censoring via max_time. Binary covariates can specified index via binary_idx. variables generated using latent Gaussian threshold model achieve desired prevalence approximate within-binary correlation controlled rho_binary. Specifically, \(B\) binary \(P(B=1)=p\), generated \(B = (L > c)\) \(L\) standard normal \(c=\Phi^{-1}(1-p)\). multiple binary covariates requested, latent variables generated jointly equicorrelation rho_binary. controls latent (tetrachoric) correlation; resulting Pearson correlation among binary variables constrained prevalence generally close identical rho_binary. ties=TRUE, observed times discretized ties_levels bins (based sample quantiles) replaced bin midpoints induce tied event/censoring times. Smaller ties_levels produces stronger ties.

text: n_stratum Integer. Number strata. n.beta Integer. Total number covariates \(p\). beta_value_vec Numeric vector. True coefficients first length(beta_value_vec) covariates. Remaining coefficients (n.beta) set 0. beta_idx Integer vector NULL. Indices (1:n.beta) covariates nonzero true coefficients. NULL, defaults 1:length(beta_value_vec) (original behavior). Must length beta_value_vec filtering valid indices. mu_Z Numeric vector NULL. Mean vector continuous covariates. NULL, zero vector used. indices binary_idx, mu_Z ignored. sd_Z Numeric NULL. Standard deviations continuous covariates. Four shapes accepted: NULL (default; standard deviations set 1), scalar (recycled n.beta covariates), vector length n.beta (used -), vector length equal number continuous covariates (.e. length(setdiff(1:n.beta, binary_idx)), applied positions 1 elsewhere). values must positive finite. Standard deviations binary_idx positions effect, since binary covariates generated latent threshold model. stratum_size Integer numeric vector. Stratum sample sizes. scalar, recycled length n_stratum; vector, must length n_stratum. rho Numeric. Correlation parameter \([0,1)\) equicorrelation covariance structure used generate continuous covariates. censor_rate Numeric. Target random censoring rate \([0,1)\). 0, random censoring applied (administrative censoring via max_time may still apply). censor_type Character. Random censoring distribution. One "uniform", "exponential", "weibull", "lognormal", "none". max_time Numeric. Administrative censoring time. Observed time min(event, censor, max_time). seed Integer NULL. Random seed reproducibility. baseline Character. Baseline hazard type. One "exponential" "weibull". alpha Numeric NULL. Required baseline="weibull". Controls Weibull baseline hazard \(h_0(t)=\alpha t\); must positive finite. Ignored baseline="exponential". censor_weibull_shape Numeric. Log-scale standard deviation \(\sigma_c>0\) log-normal random censoring censor_type="lognormal". mean log scale calibrated internally match censor_rate. Ignored otherwise. binary_idx Integer vector. Indices (1:n.beta) covariates generated binary. Default none (covariates continuous). binary_prev Numeric scalar vector. Prevalence \(P(Z_j=1)\) binary covariates. scalar, recycled binary covariates. Must \((0,1)\). rho_binary Numeric. Equicorrelation parameter \([0,1)\) latent Gaussian vector used generate binary covariates. Ignored binary_idx empty. ties Logical. TRUE, discretize observed times induce ties. ties_levels Integer. Number bins used discretize time ties=TRUE. Smaller values yield stronger ties. Must \(\ge 2\).

title: Evaluate NCC Model: Loss, C-Index, and Brier Score — test_eval_ncc
text: Numeric performance metric. "loss": \(-2\) times conditional log-partial likelihood divided number matched sets. Note Cox counterpart test_eval divides "loss" number subjects, two losses different scales must compared directly. "CIndex": despite name, matched-set AUC (pair-weighted average within-set case-versus-control rank comparisons). 1:M matched sets matched-set concordance index matched-set AUC coincide, two names used interchangeably . "Brier": mean squared difference case indicator within-set multinomial probability implied linear predictor.
